body:
## Summary

`reflex run --env prod` and `reflex export` previously required a paid tier (Pro, Team, Enterprise). A logged-in **Free** account can now run both, provided the app shows the "Built with Reflex" badge.

| | Logged out | Free | Pro / Team / Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reflex run` (dev) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `reflex run --env prod` | ❌ | ✅ with badge | ✅ |
| `reflex export` | ❌ | ✅ with badge | ✅ |

## Changes

- `check_paid_tier_for_command` allows non-paid, logged-in tiers when `show_built_with_reflex` is on. Logged-out users get a `reflex login` error; a Free user with the badge off gets an error pointing at the badge or an upgrade.
- `AppEnterprise.__post_init__` runs `_verify_and_setup_badge` before the command check, so the check sees the enforced badge value. Free cannot hide the badge, so in practice Free prod runs and exports always pass once logged in.
- Exports now always include the badge when it is enabled, including `reflex export --env dev`, which previously built without it (the badge was only added in prod mode).
- README licensing section and a news fragment updated.

## Reflex Cloud

Cloud (flexgen) builds the frontend with `reflex deploy` and runs the backend with `reflex run --env prod --backend-only`, using an app token that reports the owning org's tier. Before this change, a Free-org reflex-enterprise app would hit the paid-tier check at backend startup; it now starts with the badge.

Not changed here: a Pro app hiding the badge on Cloud still logs a misleading "restricted" warning at runtime, because the runtime uses the `RUN` context where only Team/Enterprise may hide it. The deployed frontend is unaffected.

## Testing

- `test_check_paid_tier_for_command` covers Free with/without the badge for both prod runs and exports.
- New `test_badge_setup` checks the badge is added for prod runs and dev-mode exports, and not for dev runs.
- `pytest tests/units`: 1163 passed; ruff and pyright clean.
title: feat: allow Free-tier prod runs and exports with the badge
